newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen unable to top $328 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen unable to top $328 resistance.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold prices look like remaining in their $321-$328 per ounce range on Monday as the market digs in ahead of the over the counter (OTC) option expiry on Tuesday.
Some analysts said silver's prospects might be more positive but resistance at $4.40 would have to be taken out first.
GOLD
Analysts and dealers said the precious metals would be marking time ahead of the option expiry, which would help confine gold's ambitions.
Producer selling and profit-taking were assisting the resistance at $328/$329, where the market had failed three times recently.
Support was expected at $324 initially and then at $321.
"There is no real trend. We are in a fairly narrow range and that is likely to remain in place until after the expiry," one analyst said.
Above the market, $332-$333 was the next significant area, which was a 40 percent retracement level.
However, gold was technically still close to oversold with an RSI of 52, which might encourage some covering.
"The action is still with the shorts and they are in no hurry to take their profits. The funds hold the key and the investors are staying away," one analyst said.
The $320, $325 and $330 strike prices were the most significant major numbers for the options expiry.
"There has been a tendancy for the market to turn lower after expiries," an analyst observed.
At 0740 GMT gold was indicated at $325.25/$325.75 compared with London's $323.80/$324.30 finish on Friday.
SILVER
Further gains were forecast for silver, where the technical indicators were turning higher.

A constructive close on Friday of $4.31/$4.33 and $4.315, up four cents on the Comex September contract, suggested the $4.40 spot resistance could be challenged later this week when the option expiry was completed.
"Silver got from $4.37 to $4.45 for a moment last week but there was no follow through buying," one analyst said.
However, he added, "The (gold/silver) ratio is getting better for silver. I would be prepared to sell gold and buy silver."
The gold/silver ratio was at 75.15 on Friday, off last Tuesday's high of 76.61 but well above early July levels of around 71/72.
At 0740 silver was indicated at $4.34/$4.36, up three cents from Friday's close.
PLATINUM
The market was nervous but quiet on Monday morning with prices barely moving from $423.00/$426.00, just 50 cents up on the Friday close.
Options were also an issue for platinum, which was still tight and in steep backwardation despite the first arrivals of Russia metal in Tokyo last week.
Resistance was likely near the current price, and the July 1 high of $437.00 was likely to stop any breakout attempt, analysts said.
Buying would support at $410.00.
At 0840 platinum was indicated at $423.00/$426.00, just 50 cents above London's Friday close.
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
